html:
Black January was the storming of Baku by Soviet troops on the night of 19 to 20 January 1990, in which about 130 to 150 civilians were killed.

Tension over Karabakh had brought the Popular Front of Azerbaijan to the edge of power, and a pogrom against Armenians in Baku a week earlier gave Moscow its reason. Gorbachev declared a state of emergency, and troops broke through barricades and fired on crowds and cars. Hundreds were wounded. Instead of saving Soviet rule, the attack turned most Azerbaijanis against the Soviet Union. Tens of thousands handed in their party cards, and Azerbaijan declared independence the next year. 20 January is a day of national mourning in Azerbaijan.
sum: Black January was the storming of Baku by Soviet troops on the night of 19 to 20 January 1990, in which about 130 to 150 civilians were killed.
